title: The Still-Warm Camp
text: A camp, its fire still smouldering, its packs still full, a pot of something going cold on the stones. Bedrolls lie thrown back. Whoever left did so in a hurry, meaning to return. They have not, and the woods around are very quiet.

options.label: Take what they left behind. They will not be needing it.

outcomes.text: You gather timber, iron and a little gold. No one returns to claim it.
The owners return for it. Not all of them are the people who left, nor are all of them people.

options.label: Leave it be and walk softly. Whatever they fled may still be near.

outcomes.text: Whoever left the camp returns that night, finds the ground disturbed and follows your tracks.
An hour later you hear screaming from the direction of the camp. Whatever they fled has caught them instead of you.
Further on you find a cairn stacked neatly beside the path, left as a gift from strangers or perhaps as thanks from the woods.

options.label: The Vagabond goes through the packs, quickly and quietly, before anyone returns.

outcomes.text: The Vagabond's quick hands fill their pockets. Whoever returns for these packs will find them light.
In the last pack the Vagabond finds a letter addressed to them by name, written in their own hand.
